---
title: API overview and authentication
description: "Reaching Pi Durable Platform agents from your own app: the three kinds of credentials, which routes take which, the response envelope, revisions, and choosing between a service account and OAuth Connect."
---

Your app reaches Pi Durable Platform's agents through its HTTP API, at the platform's `APP_URL` (here `https://agents.example.com`). The app never talks to an agent's runtime: it sends messages to the platform and follows the conversation as server-sent events.

```sh
# Start a thread (the platform chooses its ID), send a message (202), then follow the thread
THREAD=$(curl -s -X POST https://agents.example.com/v1/agents/$AGENT/threads \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PDP_KEY" | jq -r .data.threadId)
curl -X POST https://agents.example.com/v1/agents/$AGENT/threads/$THREAD/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PDP_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text": "Hello", "requestId": "m1"}'
curl -N https://agents.example.com/v1/agents/$AGENT/threads/$THREAD/events \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PDP_KEY"
```

## Credentials

Send one as `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`.

| Credential | Prefix | Acts as | Get it from |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Service account key** | `pdp_sa_` | The team's service account, in its own team, with its role (member or editor) | A team owner or admin: [Service accounts](/docs/teams/service-accounts) |
| **Personal API key** | `pdp_` | A person, with their access | The person: [API keys](/docs/use/api-keys) |
| **OAuth Connect access token** | `pdpat_` | A person who connected your app, **without** their platform role | [OAuth Connect](/docs/build/oauth-connect) |

### Which to use

- **Your app acts for itself**, for example giving each of its users an agent of their own inside your team: a **service account**. The conversations belong to the app; see [Agents by key](/docs/build/agents-by-key).
- **Your app acts for a person** (their personal workspace, their teams' agents, their private threads): **OAuth Connect**. The person signs in to the platform once and allows your app.
- **A person's own script**: a personal API key.

Both service-account mode and OAuth Connect are supported; an app can offer both, and use OAuth Connect where the platform advertises it (`connect` in `GET /v1/auth/config`).

### Which routes take which credentials

Bearer credentials reach the **agent routes** and a few readings:

- agents, threads, messages, events and thread MCP servers (`/v1/agents…`, `/v1/teams/{team}/agents…`);
- template listings (`GET /v1/agent-templates`, the team's templates);
- a team's models, usage, limits and MCP servers;
- `GET /v1/me`, `GET /v1/teams` and `GET /v1/teams/{team}`, for people only: a service account key gets `403 person_required`.

Everything else (administration, members, invites, creating keys, service accounts, connected apps, consent) needs a **browser session**. `PUT …/agents/by-key/…` is for service accounts only.

## Conventions

- **Envelope**: success is `{"data": …}`; an error is `{"error": {"code": "…", "message": "…"}}` with an HTTP status. See [Errors and limits](/docs/build/errors-and-limits).
- **Request IDs**: every response has `X-Request-ID`. Quote it when you report a problem; it's in the platform's logs and audit log.
- **Not allowed looks like not found**: an agent or thread the caller may not use answers `404`, the same as one that doesn't exist.
- **Revisions**: objects that can be edited carry a `revision`, returned as `ETag`. `PATCH` sends it back as `If-Match`: missing is `428 revision_required`, stale is `412 revision_conflict`.
- **IDs** are UUIDs. Teams also have slugs; routes with `{team}` take either.
- **Times** are RFC 3339 strings in resources, and Unix milliseconds in conversations (`at`, `createdAt` of threads, …).
- **Browser sessions** also need `X-CSRF-Token` (from `GET /v1/me`) and a same-origin `Origin` on writes. Bearer requests need neither.

## Checking a credential

```sh
curl https://agents.example.com/v1/me -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

For a person, it returns who they are, their groups, their teams and their capabilities (always false for an app's token). It wakes no agent. For a service account, use `GET /v1/agents` instead.
